decision: Create petzkod5/rsdw-c2 as a focused first draft
why: The requested first release omits backups and integrations and concentrates on metrics, logs, uptime, restart, image updates, and update detection

decision: Use one Go stdlib service with embedded static UI and Helm/kubectl orchestration
why: The API model, UI actions, and Kubernetes contract share one boundary; a single owner keeps the mutation path auditable

decision: Persist server state as a small atomic JSON journal
why: The platform needs restart-safe inventory and event history without adding a database dependency

decision: Apply a dense dark operations-console design with accessible controls
why: The supplied mockups call for an operator-first console; the design system adds visible focus, semantic status colors, and reduced-motion support

decision: Expose dashboard, telemetry, events, and maintenance flows
why: These pages cover the requested first-draft lifecycle while intentionally leaving backups and integrations out

decision: Serve embedded web assets from the embedded web root
why: The first local check exposed a filesystem-root mismatch; fs.Sub now serves the actual UI root

decision: Generate an in-cluster kubeconfig when the service-account environment is present
why: The Helm deployment runs inside Kubernetes and needs Helm/kubectl to authenticate without a host kubeconfig
result: VERIFIED by unit and render checks

decision: Require an admin token outside demo mode and at chart install time
why: The service can create, restart, update, and read server data; unauthenticated production access is unsafe
result: VERIFIED by auth tests and required-secret render checks

decision: Refresh live game health, player count, uptime, and registry semver tags
why: Stored demo values cannot represent the live server; the operator needs current state before acting
result: VERIFIED by API command, telemetry, and semver tests

decision: Exercise each visible UI action through a browser pass
why: The request requires no inert controls; the browser matrix records the observed route, modal, toast, or state transition for each control

decision: Run a one-control-plane kind deployment smoke test
why: Kubernetes deployment behavior should be tested, but Docker is unavailable to this workspace and the remote context must not be touched
